page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM-based cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. The system features 32 dedicated physical cores running on 32 vCPUs with an ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture clocked at 3.3 GHz. Each core provides 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, supported by a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128 GB of RAM, establishing a 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes 1900 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a 17 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and memory subsystem throughput. In multi-core testing, the instance scored 25,006 in Geekbench and 64,195.97 in stress-ng multi-core metrics, both falling into the upper performance tiers. Single-threaded capabilities are reflected in a Geekbench score of 2,302, with top-tier marks in clang compilation (62,134.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (36.47 GB/sec). Memory benchmarks register top-tier performance in PassMark memory testing (4,567.63) and cached read bandwidth (4,272.72 GB/sec), alongside 45,874.73 points in PassMark database operations and 94.77 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:1 ratio between physical cores and vCPUs eliminates hardware hyper-threading contention, resulting in consistent multi-threaded compute. Coupled with bundled 1.9 TB high-speed local NVMe storage and balanced memory, the instance delivers high compute efficiency per core for data-heavy workloads. It is structurally well-suited for high-throughput relational databases, in-memory caching layers, static web serving clusters, large-scale CI/CD software compilation pipelines, and transactional backend applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs built on the 3.3 GHz ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V3 architecture. It includes 128 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4 GB per core allocation, paired with 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 17 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core compilation, database operations, and data compression benchmarks, supported by high memory bandwidth and absence of simultaneous multithreading overhead. While CPU-bound single-thread stress-ng runs and small-model LLM inference register in average benchmark percentiles, the system offers efficient parallel performance. This profile makes the instance well suited for database engines, Redis caching tiers, code compilation pipelines, and transactional web serving workloads.
